verses.english: Middle Discourses 50
The Condemnation of Māra
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahāmoggallāno abbhokāse caṅkamati.
verses.english: At that time Moggallāna was walking mindfully in the open air.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena māro pāpimā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa kucchigato hoti koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭho.
verses.english: Now at that time Māra the Wicked had got inside Moggallāna’s belly.
Moggallāna thought,

verses.pali: “kiṁ nu kho me kucchi garugaro viya?
verses.english: “Why now is my belly so very heavy,
like I’ve just eaten a load of beans?”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno caṅkamā orohitvā vihāraṁ pavisitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
verses.english: Then he stepped down from the walking path, entered his dwelling, sat down on the seat spread out,

verses.pali: Nisajja kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno paccattaṁ yoniso manasākāsi.
verses.english: and investigated inside himself.

verses.pali: Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṁ pāpimantaṁ kucchigataṁ koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭhaṁ.
verses.english: He saw that Māra the Wicked had got inside his belly.
So he said to Māra,
“Come out, Wicked One,
come out!
Do not harass the Realized One or his disciple.

verses.pali: Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā”ti.
verses.english: Don’t create lasting harm and suffering for yourself!”
Then Māra thought,

verses.pali: “ajānameva kho maṁ ayaṁ samaṇo apassaṁ evamāha:
verses.english: “This ascetic doesn’t really know me or see me when he tells me to come out.

verses.pali: Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti.
Yopissa so satthā sopi maṁ neva khippaṁ jāneyya, kuto pana maṁ ayaṁ sāvako jānissatī”ti?
verses.english: Not even the Teacher could recognize me so quickly, so how could a disciple?”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṁ pāpimantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Moggallāna said to Māra,

verses.pali: “evampi kho tāhaṁ, pāpima, jānāmi, mā tvaṁ maññittho:
verses.english: “I know you even when you’re like this, Wicked One. Do not think,
‘He doesn’t know me.’
You are Māra the Wicked.
And you think,

verses.pali: ‘ajānameva kho maṁ ayaṁ samaṇo apassaṁ evamāha—
verses.english: ‘This ascetic doesn’t really know me or see me when he tells me to come out.

verses.pali: Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyāti.
Yopissa so satthā sopi maṁ neva khippaṁ jāneyya, kuto pana maṁ ayaṁ sāvako jānissatī’”ti?
verses.english: Not even the Teacher could recognize me so quickly, so how could a disciple?’”
Then Māra thought,

verses.pali: “jānameva kho maṁ ayaṁ samaṇo passaṁ evamāha:
verses.english: “This ascetic really does know me and see me when he tells me to come out.”

verses.pali: Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā’”ti.
Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa mukhato uggantvā paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: Then Māra came up out of Moggallāna’s mouth and stood against the door.

verses.pali: Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṁ pāpimantaṁ paccaggaḷe ṭhitaṁ;
verses.english: Moggallāna saw him there
and said,

verses.pali: “etthāpi kho tāhaṁ, pāpima, passāmi; mā tvaṁ maññittho
verses.english: “I see you even there, Wicked One. Do not think,
‘He doesn’t see me.’
That’s you, Wicked One, standing against the door.

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, pāpima, dūsī nāma māro ahosiṁ, tassa me kāḷī nāma bhaginī.
verses.english: Once upon a time, Wicked One, I was a Māra named Dūsī, and I had a sister named Kāḷī.
You were her son,
which made you my nephew.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, pāpima, samayena kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti.
verses.english: At that time Kakusandha, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha arose in the world.

verses.pali: Kakusandhassa kho pana, pāpima, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa vidhurasañjīvaṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ ahosi aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
verses.english: Kakusandha had a fine pair of chief disciples named Vidhura and Sañjīva.

verses.pali: Yāvatā kho pana, pāpima, kakusandhassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa sāvakā.
verses.english: Of all the disciples of the Buddha Kakusandha,

verses.pali: Tesu na ca koci āyasmatā vidhurena samasamo hoti yadidaṁ dhammadesanāya.
verses.english: none were the equal of Venerable Vidhura in teaching Dhamma.

verses.pali: Iminā kho evaṁ, pāpima, pariyāyena āyasmato vidhurassa vidhuroteva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And that’s how he came to be known as Vidhura.

verses.pali: Āyasmā pana, pāpima, sañjīvo araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi appakasireneva saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjati.
verses.english: But when Venerable Sañjīva had gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he easily attained the cessation of perception and feeling.

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, pāpima, āyasmā sañjīvo aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpanno nisinno hoti.
verses.english: Once upon a time, Sañjīva was sitting at the root of a certain tree having attained the cessation of perception and feeling.

verses.pali: Addasaṁsu kho, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino āyasmantaṁ sañjīvaṁ aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpannaṁ nisinnaṁ;
verses.english: Some cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and passers-by saw him sitting there
and said,
‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!
This ascetic passed away while seated.
We should cremate him.’

verses.pali: Atha kho te, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino tiṇañca kaṭṭhañca gomayañca saṅkaḍḍhitvā āyasmato sañjīvassa kāye upacinitvā aggiṁ datvā pakkamiṁsu.
verses.english: They collected grass, wood, and cow-dung, heaped it all on Sañjīva’s body, set it on fire, and left.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, āyasmā sañjīvo tassā rattiyā accayena tāya samāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā cīvarāni papphoṭetvā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
verses.english: Then, when the night had passed, Sañjīva emerged from that attainment, shook out his robes, and, since it was morning, he robed up and entered the village for alms.

verses.pali: Addasaṁsu kho te, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino āyasmantaṁ sañjīvaṁ piṇḍāya carantaṁ;
verses.english: Those cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and passers-by saw him wandering for alms
and said,
‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!

verses.pali: Ayaṁ samaṇo nisinnakova kālaṅkato, svāyaṁ paṭisañjīvito’ti.
verses.english: This ascetic passed away while seated, and now he has come back to life!’

verses.pali: Iminā kho evaṁ, pāpima, pariyāyena āyasmato sañjīvassa sañjīvoteva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And that’s how he came to be known as Sañjīva.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, dūsissa mārassa etadahosi:
verses.english: Then it occurred to Māra Dūsī,

verses.pali: ‘imesaṁ kho ahaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ sīlavantānaṁ kalyāṇadhammānaṁ neva jānāmi āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā.
verses.english: ‘I don’t know the course of rebirth of these ethical mendicants of good character.
Why don’t I take possession of these brahmins and householders and say,

verses.pali: etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha.
verses.english: “Come, all of you, abuse, attack, harass, and trouble the ethical mendicants of good character.

verses.pali: Appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṁ paribhāsiyamānānaṁ rosiyamānānaṁ vihesiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran’ti.
verses.english: Hopefully by doing this we can upset their minds so that Māra Dūsī can find a vulnerability.”’

verses.pali: Atha kho te, pāpima, dūsī māro brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāvisi:
verses.english: And that’s exactly what he did.

verses.pali: ‘etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha.
Appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṁ paribhāsiyamānānaṁ rosiyamānānaṁ vihesiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran’ti.
Atha kho te, pāpima, brāhmaṇagahapatikā anvāvisiṭṭhā dūsinā mārena bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti:
verses.english: Then those brahmins and householders abused, attacked, harassed, and troubled the ethical mendicants of good character:

verses.pali: ‘ime pana muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā “jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā”ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti.
verses.english: ‘These shavelings, fake ascetics, primitives, black spawn from the feet of our kinsman, say, “We practice absorption meditation! We practice absorption meditation!” Shoulders drooping, downcast, and dopey, they meditate and concentrate and contemplate and ruminate.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma ulūko rukkhasākhāyaṁ mūsikaṁ maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati;
verses.english: They’re just like an owl on a branch, which meditates and concentrates and contemplates and ruminates as it hunts a mouse.

verses.pali: evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā “jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā”ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti.
Seyyathāpi nāma kotthu nadītīre macche maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati;
verses.english: They’re just like a jackal on a river-bank, which meditates and concentrates and contemplates and ruminates as it hunts a fish.

verses.pali: evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā “jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā”ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti.
Seyyathāpi nāma biḷāro sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīre mūsikaṁ maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati;
verses.english: They’re just like a cat by an alley or a drain or a dustbin, which meditates and concentrates and contemplates and ruminates as it hunts a mouse.

verses.pali: evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā “jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā”ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti.
Seyyathāpi nāma gadrabho vahacchinno sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīre jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati;
verses.english: They’re just like an unladen donkey by an alley or a drain or a dustbin, which meditates and concentrates and contemplates and ruminates.

verses.pali: evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā “jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā”ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyantī’ti.
verses.english: In the same way, these shavelings, fake ascetics, primitives, black spawn from the feet of our kinsman, say, “We practice absorption meditation! We practice absorption meditation!” Shoulders drooping, downcast, and dopey, they meditate and concentrate and contemplate and ruminate.’

verses.pali: Ye kho pana, pāpima, tena samayena manussā kālaṁ karonti yebhuyyena kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
verses.english: Most of the people who died at that time—when their body broke up, after death—were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Kakusandha the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, addressed the mendicants:
‘Mendicants, the brahmins and householders have been possessed by Māra Dūsī.

verses.pali: etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha, appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṁ paribhāsiyamānānaṁ rosiyamānānaṁ vihesiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran’ti.
verses.english: He told them to abuse you in the hope of upsetting your minds so that he can find a vulnerability.

verses.pali: Etha, tumhe, bhikkhave, mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharatha.
verses.english: Come, all of you mendicants, meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
Meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …
Meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing …

verses.pali: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharathā’ti.
verses.english: Meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.’

verses.pali: Atha kho te, pāpima, bhikkhū kakusandhena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena evaṁ ovadiyamānā evaṁ anusāsiyamānā araññagatāpi rukkhamūlagatāpi suññāgāragatāpi mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā vihariṁsu, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā vihariṁsu.
verses.english: When those mendicants were instructed and advised by the Buddha Kakusandha in this way, they went to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, where they meditated spreading a heart full of love …
compassion …
rejoicing …

verses.pali: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā vihariṁsu, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā vihariṁsu.
verses.english: equanimity.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, dūsissa mārassa etadahosi:
verses.english: Then it occurred to Māra Dūsī,

verses.pali: ‘evampi kho ahaṁ karonto imesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ sīlavantānaṁ kalyāṇadhammānaṁ neva jānāmi āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā, yannūnāhaṁ brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāviseyyaṁ:
verses.english: ‘Even when I do this I don’t know the course of rebirth of these ethical mendicants of good character. Why don’t I take possession of these brahmins and householders and say,

verses.pali: “etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṁ karotha mānetha pūjetha,
verses.english: “Come, all of you, honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the ethical mendicants of good character.

verses.pali: appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṁ garukariyamānānaṁ māniyamānānaṁ pūjiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran”’ti.
verses.english: Hopefully by doing this we can upset their minds so that Māra Dūsī can find a vulnerability.”’

verses.pali: Atha kho te, pāpima, dūsī māro brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāvisi:
verses.english: And that’s exactly what he did.

verses.pali: ‘etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṁ karotha mānetha pūjetha,
appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṁ garukariyamānānaṁ māniyamānānaṁ pūjiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran’ti.
Atha kho te, pāpima, brāhmaṇagahapatikā anvāviṭṭhā dūsinā mārena bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti.
verses.english: Then those brahmins and householders honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated the ethical mendicants of good character.

verses.pali: Ye kho pana, pāpima, tena samayena manussā kālaṁ karonti yebhuyyena kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
verses.english: Most of the people who died at that time—when their body broke up, after death—were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Kakusandha the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, addressed the mendicants:
‘Mendicants, the brahmins and householders have been possessed by Māra Dūsī.

verses.pali: “etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṁ karotha mānetha pūjetha,
verses.english: He told them to venerate you

verses.pali: appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṁ garukariyamānānaṁ māniyamānānaṁ pūjiyamānānaṁ siyā cittassa aññathattaṁ, yathā taṁ dūsī māro labhetha otāran”ti.
verses.english: in the hope of upsetting your minds so that he can find a vulnerability.

verses.pali: Etha, tumhe, bhikkhave, asubhānupassino kāye viharatha, āhāre paṭikūlasaññino, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññino, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassino’ti.
verses.english: Come, all you mendicants, meditate observing the ugliness of the body, perceiving the repulsiveness of food, perceiving dissatisfaction with the whole world, and observing the impermanence of all conditions.’

verses.pali: Atha kho te, pāpima, bhikkhū kakusandhena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena evaṁ ovadiyamānā evaṁ anusāsiyamānā araññagatāpi rukkhamūlagatāpi suññāgāragatāpi asubhānupassino kāye vihariṁsu, āhāre paṭikūlasaññino, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññino, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassino.
verses.english: When those mendicants were instructed and advised by the Buddha Kakusandha in this way, they went to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, where they meditated observing the ugliness of the body, perceiving the repulsiveness of food, perceiving dissatisfaction with the whole world, and observing the impermanence of all conditions.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā vidhurena pacchāsamaṇena gāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha Kakusandha robed up in the morning and, taking this bowl and robe, entered the village for alms with Venerable Vidhura as his second monk.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, dūsī māro aññataraṁ kumārakaṁ anvāvisitvā sakkharaṁ gahetvā āyasmato vidhurassa sīse pahāramadāsi; sīsaṁ vobhindi.
verses.english: Then Māra Dūsī took possession of a certain boy, picked up a rock, and hit Vidhura on the head, cracking it open.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, āyasmā vidhuro bhinnena sīsena lohitena gaḷantena kakusandhaṁyeva bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi.
verses.english: Then Vidhura, with blood pouring from his cracked skull, still followed behind the Buddha Kakusandha.

verses.pali: Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho nāgāpalokitaṁ apalokesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha Kakusandha turned to gaze back, the way that elephants do, saying,
‘This Māra Dūsī knows no limit.’

verses.pali: Sahāpalokanāya ca pana, pāpima, dūsī māro tamhā ca ṭhānā cavi mahānirayañca upapajji.
verses.english: And as he was gazing, Māra Dūsī fell from that place and was reborn in the Great Hell.

verses.pali: Tassa kho pana, pāpima, mahānirayassa tayo nāmadheyyā honti—
verses.english: Now that Great Hell is known by three names:

verses.pali: chaphassāyataniko itipi, saṅkusamāhato itipi, paccattavedaniyo itipi.
verses.english: ‘Related to the Six Fields of Contact’ and also ‘The Impaling With Spikes’ and also ‘Uniquely Painful’.

verses.pali: Atha kho maṁ, pāpima, nirayapālā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then the wardens of hell came to me and said,

verses.pali: ‘yadā kho te, mārisa, saṅkunā saṅku hadaye samāgaccheyya.
verses.english: ‘When spike meets spike in your heart,
you will know that
you’ve been roasting in hell for a thousand years.’

verses.pali: So kho ahaṁ, pāpima, bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni tasmiṁ mahāniraye apacciṁ.
verses.english: I roasted for many years, many centuries, many millennia in that Great Hell.

verses.pali: Dasavassasahassāni tasseva mahānirayassa ussade apacciṁ vuṭṭhānimaṁ nāma vedanaṁ vediyamāno.
verses.english: For ten thousand years I roasted in the annex of that Great Hell, experiencing the pain called ‘this is emergence’.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, pāpima, evarūpo kāyo hoti, seyyathāpi manussassa.
verses.english: My body was in human form,
but I had the head of a fish.
What kind of hell was that,
where Dūsī was roasted
after attacking the disciple Vidhura
along with the brahmin Kakusandha?
There were 100 iron spikes,
each one uniquely painful.
That’s the kind of hell
where Dūsī was roasted
after attacking the disciple Vidhura
along with the brahmin Kakusandha.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
There are mansions that last an eon
standing in the middle of a lake.
Sapphire-colored, brilliant,
they sparkle and shine.
Dancing there are nymphs
shining in all different colors.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
I’m the one who, urged by the Buddha,
shook the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother
with his big toe
as the Saṅgha of mendicants watched.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
I’m the one who shook the Palace of Victory
with his big toe
owing to psychic power,
inspiring deities to awe.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
I’m the one who asked Sakka
in the Palace of Victory:
‘Vāsava, I hope you recall
the one who is freed through the ending of craving?’
And I’m the one to whom Sakka
admitted the truth when asked.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
I’m the one who asked the Divinity
in the Hall of Clear Right before the assembly:
‘Respectable sir, do you still have the same view
that you had in the past?
Or do you see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity?’
And I’m the one to whom the Divinity
truthfully admitted his progress:
‘Good fellow, I don’t have that view
that I had in the past.
I see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity.
So how could I say today
that I am permanent and eternal?’
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
I’m the one who touched the peak of Mount Meru
using the power of meditative liberation.
I’ve visited the forests of the people
who dwell in the land east of Videha.
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.
Though a fire doesn’t think,
‘I’ll burn the fool!’
Still the fool who attacks
the fire gets burnt.
In the same way, Māra,
in attacking the Realized One,
you’ll only burn yourself,
like a fool touching the flames.
Māra’s done a bad thing
in attacking the Realized One.
Wicked One, do you imagine that
your wickedness won’t bear fruit?
Your deeds heap up wickedness
that will last a long time, terminator!
Give up on the Buddha, Māra!
And hold no hope for the mendicants!”
That is how, in the Bhesekaḷā grove,
the mendicant condemned Māra.
That spirit, downcast,
disappeared right there.

verses.pali: Dūsī ca māro dasamo ca vaggo.
